```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = TRUE
)

data("instacart", package = "p8105.datasets")

# Each row is a product within an order, rather than an entire order.
shopping_data = instacart %>%
  select(
    order_id, product_id, department, aisle,
    order_hour_of_day, reordered
  )

department_summary = shopping_data %>%
  count(department, name = "product_rows", sort = TRUE)

department_top = department_summary %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)

# Count each order only once when describing order timing.
order_data = shopping_data %>%
  distinct(order_id, order_hour_of_day)

hour_summary = order_data %>%
  count(order_hour_of_day, name = "orders") %>%
  arrange(order_hour_of_day)

aisle_summary = shopping_data %>%
  group_by(aisle) %>%
  summarise(
    product_rows = n(),
    unique_products = n_distinct(product_id),
    known_reorder_rows = sum(!is.na(reordered)),
    reordered_rows = sum(reordered == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    reorder_rate = reordered_rows / na_if(known_reorder_rows, 0)
  )

# The minimum denominator is an exploratory display choice.
aisle_plot_data = aisle_summary %>%
  filter(known_reorder_rows >= 100, !is.na(reorder_rate))

top_department = department_top %>%
  slice_head(n = 1)

peak_hours = hour_summary %>%
  filter(orders == max(orders))

dataset_summary = tibble::tibble(
  Measure = c("Product records", "Distinct orders", "Distinct products"),
  Value = c(
    nrow(shopping_data),
    n_distinct(shopping_data$order_id),
    n_distinct(shopping_data$product_id)
  )
)
```
Row {data-height=460}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Top 10 departments by product records

```{r department-bar}
department_plot = plotly::plot_ly(
  data = department_top,
  x = ~product_rows,
  y = ~department,
  type = "bar",
  orientation = "h",
  marker = list(color = "#287C8E"),
  hovertemplate = paste0(
    "Department: %{y}<br>",
    "Product records: %{x:,}<extra></extra>"
  )
) %>%
  plotly::layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "Product records", tickformat = ",d"),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "",
      categoryorder = "array",
      categoryarray = rev(department_top$department),
      automargin = TRUE
    ),
    margin = list(l = 150, r = 25, t = 20, b = 65),
    font = list(size = 14),
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) %>%
  plotly::config(displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)

department_plot
```
### Distinct orders by hour of day

```{r hourly-line}
hour_plot = plotly::plot_ly(
  data = hour_summary,
  x = ~order_hour_of_day,
  y = ~orders,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines+markers",
  line = list(color = "#D77529", width = 3),
  marker = list(color = "#D77529", size = 7),
  hovertemplate = paste0(
    "Hour: %{x}:00<br>",
    "Distinct orders: %{y:,}<extra></extra>"
  )
) %>%
  plotly::layout(
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Hour of day (0–23)",
      tickmode = "linear",
      tick0 = 0,
      dtick = 3,
      range = c(-0.5, 23.5)
    ),
    yaxis = list(title = "Distinct orders", tickformat = ",d"),
    margin = list(l = 80, r = 25, t = 20, b = 65),
    font = list(size = 14),
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) %>%
  plotly::config(displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)

hour_plot
```
Row {data-height=500}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Aisle-level purchasing and reordering

```{r aisle-scatter}
aisle_plot = plotly::plot_ly(
  data = aisle_plot_data,
  x = ~product_rows,
  y = ~reorder_rate,
  text = ~aisle,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  marker = list(
    color = "#6153A3",
    size = 10,
    opacity = 0.75,
    line = list(color = "white", width = 0.5)
  ),
  hovertemplate = paste0(
    "Aisle: %{text}<br>",
    "Product records: %{x:,}<br>",
    "Reorder rate: %{y:.1%}<extra></extra>"
  )
) %>%
  plotly::layout(
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Product records (log scale)",
      type = "log",
      tickformat = ",d"
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Reorder rate",
      tickformat = ".0%",
      range = c(0, 1)
    ),
    margin = list(l = 85, r = 25, t = 20, b = 75),
    font = list(size = 14),
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) %>%
  plotly::config(displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)

aisle_plot
```
### Data, findings, and interpretation

[Home](index.html) | [Resume](resume.html) |
[Data documentation](https://p8105.com/dataset_instacart.html)

This dashboard uses the Instacart data distributed with
`p8105.datasets`. Each row represents a product within an order.
All available records contribute to the summaries; no random sampling
is used.

```{r dataset-description}
knitr::kable(dataset_summary, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

The largest department by product records is
**`r top_department$department`**, with
**`r format(top_department$product_rows, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)`**
records. The highest observed hourly order count occurs at
**`r paste(sprintf("%02d:00", peak_hours$order_hour_of_day), collapse = ", ")`**.

The bar chart displays only the ten largest departments. The line chart
counts distinct orders, so orders with more products do not receive
extra weight. Each scatterplot point represents an aisle with at least
100 records having a known reorder indicator. Reorder rates use only
records with known reorder status in their denominators.

Hover to inspect values, drag to zoom, and double-click to reset the view.
Differences between aisles are descriptive associations and do not
establish that purchase volume causes reordering. These data are not a
random sample of all Instacart purchases, so the findings may not
generalize to all customers or time periods.
